> 天下之至柔，馳騁天下之至堅。無有入無間，吾是以知無為之有益.

Chapter 42 ended with a hard judgment: 強梁者不得其死 — the one who forces does not die a natural death.

That was a verdict without evidence. This chapter is the evidence.

It takes two things: the softest in the world, and the hardest. Then it says: the softest runs freely through the hardest.

馳騁 — not striking, not grinding, not waiting. Galloping.

And a harder line follows: what has no form enters what has no gap.

But the chapter's landing point is not "soft is powerful." It is: 吾是以知無為之有益 — this is how I know that non-forcing is beneficial.

Soft overcoming hard is the phenomenon. Non-forcing being beneficial is what he saw.

## 柔 is not soft

柔 is built on 木: the wood that can bend and straighten. It is not weakness as a lack of strength; it is the capacity to change shape without breaking.

Which is why it can run through 至堅. 至堅 is what has become a block — a thing whose shape is fixed, and therefore a thing with gaps and limits built into its fixity.

A block has edges. An edge is a place force can be applied, and also a place that can be passed.

## 無有入無間

What has no form enters what has no gap.

This is the sentence that should stop a reader. If there is no gap, how does anything enter?

The answer: only something without form. A gap is defined by a shape; a thing without form is not excluded by any boundary, because boundaries are made of form.

So the point is not that the formless is small enough to fit. It is that the formless is not subject to the boundary at all.

## 不言之教，無為之益

> 不言之教，無為之益，天下希及之.

Teaching without speech; the benefit of non-forcing. Few in the world reach it.

希 — the same word as chapter 14's unheard and chapter 41's 大音希聲. Rare, and also inaudible.

The pairing is exact: 不言之教 is what 無為 produces in others, and 無為之益 is what it produces in the situation. Both work by not presenting a form that has to be met.

## Why 無為 is not sitting still

The chapter supplies the mechanism that the phrase usually lacks.

非-forcing works because it does not create a boundary. A spoken instruction presents a form the other must accept or refuse; a forced arrangement presents a shape the situation must accommodate. Neither is neutral — both install edges.

Non-forcing installs no edge, which is why it can move through everything. It is not passivity; it is the only mode of action that has no surface to be resisted.

## A test

Take a conflict you are in. Notice how much of your effort is going into presenting a form — an argument, a demand, a position with edges. The chapter's claim is that the effort itself is what creates the wall you are pushing against.
